descriptor.scene: A close, reverent study of the portal found and open, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light standing in a small jungle clearing, soft ink-wash edge with its thin brighter rim, a few small gold motes drifting, vines drawn aside like a curtain, its lower tip floating a hand's width above the ferns, warm light spilling softly onto the forest floor. Through the opening: warm gold light and a suggestion of open sky only. One anonymous founder, small against the portal's two-person height, is caught mid-step INTO the light at its left edge, silhouetted warm, pack still on their back; a second anonymous founder waits two steps behind on the trail at the lower left, next in line. The portal fills the left-of-center of the frame and stands well clear of the exact middle; the lower right quarter is calm ferns and warm-lit trail for the caption card.
negatives: a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image
a frame, ring or machinery around the light
descriptor._caption: A portal starts wide enough for anyone who finds it. But every founder who steps through leaves it a little smaller, and every day it stands open it shrinks a little more, until one day it closes for good. The hopefuls call the time it is open a window. Rumor says the windows close faster every time.
descriptor.anonymous: two anonymous founders: one silhouetted mid-step into the light, one waiting two steps behind

prompt: Picture-book spread painted in the warm editorial ink-and-wash register of the FIRST reference image. THE FIRST REFERENCE IMAGE IS A STYLE ANCHOR ONLY. Match it for MEDIUM, BRUSHWORK, PALETTE and LIGHT QUALITY ONLY, and take NO subject from it whatsoever: none of its objects, figures, costume, props, furniture, architecture, period or location may appear in the output unless the scene description below asks for them by name. SCENE: A close, reverent study of the portal found and open, exactly as its locked master plate paints it: the tall pointed-oval of warm golden light standing in a small jungle clearing, soft ink-wash edge with its thin brighter rim, a few small gold motes drifting, vines drawn aside like a curtain, its lower tip floating a hand's width above the ferns, warm light spilling softly onto the forest floor. Through the opening: warm gold light and a suggestion of open sky only. One anonymous founder, small against the portal's two-person height, is caught mid-step INTO the light at its left edge, silhouetted warm, pack still on their back; a second anonymous founder waits two steps behind on the trail at the lower left, next in line. The portal fills the left-of-center of the frame and stands well clear of the exact middle; the lower right quarter is calm ferns and warm-lit trail for the caption card. THE CAMERA MOVES; NOTHING ELSE DOES. Every person keeps the exact seat, side and place the setting's blocking gives them, and if a BLOCKING PLATE is supplied it is the authority on who sits where: obey it at every distance. Whatever the subject is sitting at, leaning on or standing beside is STILL IN THIS PICTURE, in the near foreground if the camera is close. Everyone else present in this place is STILL PRESENT in the picture, behind or beside the subject, soft and out of focus if they are not the subject, and NOBODY leaves and NO seat empties because the camera came closer. FRAMING, THOUGHT BUBBLE. The picture has TWO parts. SMALL, at ONE EDGE of the frame and occupying no more than a quarter of it, the speaker is drawn in their real place, mid-sentence. FILLING THE REST OF THE FRAME, a single large BUBBLE holds the thing they are describing, painted as its own little scene. THE BUBBLE IS PAINTED, NOT DRAWN: its edge is a soft feathered cloud-like border of the same paint as the rest of the picture, with a few small round bubbles trailing from the speaker up to it. THE SPEAKER STAYS IN THEIR OWN SEAT on their own side of the room, and anyone sitting with them is still sitting with them. It is NEVER a hard black comic-book outline, NEVER a speech balloon with a pointed tail, NEVER a flat white shape, and it carries NO lettering of any kind. This is ONE continuous painted image containing a bubble, and it is NOT a grid, NOT split panels and NOT a comic strip. the-portal exactly as its reference plate: A doorway of pure warm light hidden in the jungle: one upright pointed-oval of warm golden light, soft-edged like wet ink-wash with a thin brighter rim, its lower tip floating a hand's width above the forest floor. No frame, no ring, no arch, no standing stones, no machinery, no doorsill: the light alone is the door. Each era gets exactly one portal, and it shrinks: the more founders pass through and the longer it stands open, the smaller it gets, until it closes and leaves a flat ring of pale gold blossoms on the forest floor. Every portal in every era is this same design at some size. This era's portal at its opening is 3.8 m tall by 2.0 m wide: about twice a person's height, so a founder walks in without ducking and an adult's head reaches only halfway up the opening. Waning, the same shape shrinks to about 1.0 m, knee-to-waist high on an adult. Closed, a flat blossom ring about 2.0 m across lies on the forest floor. The lower tip always floats a hand's width (0.15 m) above the floor. The portal stands still; it never drifts, tilts or hovers higher. State-dependent only. Hidden: hanging vines, broad leaves and leaf-shadow curtain the light so only warm slivers show through; a passerby would walk within arm's length and never know. Master (found): the vines drawn aside, the oval open and generous, warm gold light with a few small drifting motes, soft warm glow on the nearest leaves. Waning: the same portal small and low, light gentler, the green closing in around it. Closed: no light at all, a quiet flat ring of pale gold blossoms in the green, moss and ferns grown back inside it. Nothing is ever scorched, broken or ominous. At its opening, about twice a person's height and wider than a garden gate; a closed ring reads about as wide as a person is tall lying down. In a wide shot the live portal is a tall warm almond of light against the green, unmistakably person-scaled, never building-scaled and never coin-scaled. THE ONLY PEOPLE IN THIS IMAGE ARE ANONYMOUS FIGURES THIS SCENE DESCRIBES: two anonymous founders: one silhouetted mid-step into the light, one waiting two steps behind. They are ordinary unnamed people with no identity beyond what the scene says, and they are not any named character. NOBODY ELSE APPEARS. NEGATIVES: neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, glossy plastic, HUD/arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic, a second portal, second oval of light or second blossom ring anywhere in the image, crowds or queues (two founders only), a frame, ring or machinery around the light. ONE SINGLE CONTINUOUS FULL-BLEED PAINTING that fills the entire canvas edge to edge. This is NEVER a grid, NEVER a multi-panel layout, NEVER a comic page, NEVER a contact sheet, NEVER a study or turnaround sheet, NEVER a collage, and NEVER several framed views side by side. Some reference images supplied to you are multi-panel study sheets; use them ONLY for the identity and design of what they depict, and NEVER copy their panelled layout into the output. The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. HANDS. Every hand in this image has EXACTLY FOUR FINGERS AND ONE THUMB, five digits and no more and no fewer, and every person has exactly TWO hands and TWO arms. No sixth finger, no extra thumb, no duplicated or spare limb, and no hand emerging from a place no arm reaches. Two hands that come near each other stay SEPARATE and readable as two hands: they never merge into one mass, never share fingers and never fuse at the knuckles. Each hand is joined to a wrist of believable thickness, the wrist to a forearm, and the forearm to the shoulder of the person it belongs to. Hands are sized to their owner: never oversized, never doll-small. A hand resting ON something makes real contact with THAT thing, with the fingers following its actual surface and not floating above it or sinking into it.
